Generated by scripts/generate_capability_matrix.py. Source: the teardown files in `~/workspace/github-repos/ops/teardown/` (2026-11-07) for the reference side; this repo's code for our side. No date is printed here on purpose: the qa gate fails if the doc drifts from the script, and a date line would drift every day.

## How to read

- World-market capabilities first. NEPSE-only items say so in the evidence column.
- **implemented** — a tested function in this repo does it. Every such row links the test file that proves it.
- **partial** — part exists here (or in a named satellite repo) and part does not. The evidence column says which part is which.
- **not planned** — deliberately out of scope. The evidence column gives the reason, usually a programme rule: research-only, no execution, no credentials, stdlib-only, model-light.
- AGPL and unlicensed repos are ideas only: nothing was copied from them. Apache-2.0/MIT code is never pasted without attribution plus a LICENSES.md entry.

## Summary

65 headline capabilities across 15 reference repos: **29 implemented**, **22 partial**, **14 not planned**.

The implemented share is concentrated where the toolkit already lives — indicators, portfolio maths, risk measures, point-in-time discipline, decision logging — and thin where the programme deliberately stops: execution, personal finance, model zoos, and app UIs.

## Ranked build plan

Impact for a world-market user (1–5) divided by effort (1–5). Rank is the tie-break when ratios are equal. None of these is started — this table is the plan, not the work.

| Rank | Item | Impact | Effort | Impact/effort | Why here |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Universe screener | 5 | 2 | 2.50 | Highest impact per effort: the named-setup rules already exist (toolkit/terminal.py) and the scanner table exists in the satellite repo; a universe scan is a small step from both. |
| 2 | Second price source | 4 | 2 | 2.00 | Data reliability for world markets: the fallback chain in toolkit/connectors.py already supports a second source; adding one more keyless source is bounded work. |
| 3 | Volatility forecasting | 3 | 2 | 1.50 | Builds directly on toolkit/performance.py (rolling volatility) and toolkit/options.py (implied volatility): EWMA/GARCH-lite forecasts with walk-forward evaluation. |
| 4 | Opt-in macro providers (FRED/ECB/IMF) | 3 | 2 | 1.50 | PLANNED, not implemented: the FRED / ECB / IMF / SEC row stays partial (SEC EDGAR is implemented; FRED, ECB and IMF are not). An env-key FRED provider was built in Round 7.1 and then dropped by a binding constraint update, so FRED stays on the plan; keyed providers stay out of the no-key chain. |
| 5 | News and macro feed | 4 | 3 | 1.33 | Feeds the analyst agents: the EDGAR + free-data patterns exist, but a feed needs source selection, freshness rules and a sentiment-evaluation step. |
| 6 | Derivatives and fixed income | 4 | 4 | 1.00 | Extends toolkit/options.py (Black-Scholes, Greeks) to futures and bonds (duration/convexity, yield curve); a larger, self-contained build. |
| 7 | Local dashboard | 3 | 3 | 1.00 | A local HTML view over the terminal output; new surface, no new maths — behind derivatives because the maths matters more than the surface. |
| 8 | Pages demo with real global data | 3 | 4 | 0.75 | Last on purpose: it depends on the second price source and on the freshness discipline being proven, or it would publish stale data as if it were live. |

## Notes

- The scanner row (day-trader-skill) and the runbook rows (agency-agents, tradingagents) point at finance-research-agents and nepali-capital-market-research, the satellite repos where that work lives. This matrix covers this repo; the satellites have their own counts.
- The LLM provider layer (toolkit/llm_providers.py) moves two rows from 'not planned' to 'partial': structured JSON handoffs (multi-agent-market-research) and the multi-provider LLM factory (tradingagents). The executable agent team that would use it (PR B) is not in scope for this change.
